meta.triageRationale: One story in one module (the plugin's delivery board). The daemon's snapshot already gives an Epic item its own evidence with an openWith, so nothing changes on the daemon or the contract. The plugin reuses the existing Records table and the existing open path; the work is to carry the Epic's records on the Epic screen's model, draw the table there, and let the details memory open a record of the Epic on show (today it opens only the selected Story's or issue's). A few files, one clear approach, a small number of tasks.

findings.premise: The Epic's own records (DEF, HLD, epic-level amendments, SPEC) are already on the Epic item in the snapshot, so ac1 can be met from the snapshot alone with no daemon change.
findings.evidence: src/workflow/delivery/graph.ts:223-230 builds the epic draft with `evidenceArtifactIds: epicLevel.map(r => r.artifactId)`; groupKeyOf (graph.ts:42-50) puts every record with no story id under the epic-level key `${hash}|`; SPECs are appended at graph.ts:565 (`item.evidenceArtifactIds.push(r.artifactId)`). src/workflow/delivery/snapshot.ts:102-110 gives every evidence entry mdPath/openWith/approval/review, which is what ac1 (approval and review state) and ac2 (review pane vs read-only) need. The table will also list any other epic-level record (e.g. a pending EXT), which is consistent with 'the Epic's records'. [files: src/workflow/delivery/graph.ts, src/workflow/delivery/snapshot.ts]

findings.premise: Today the details memory has no selection on an Epic's board, so none of the Epic's records can be opened.
findings.evidence: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-state.ts:118-121: `return screen.kind === 'item' ? screen.itemId : null;` and board-host.ts:536 `memory.kept(shown, currentItemId(next.selection));`. details-memory.ts:164 `const item = itemId === selected ? itemOf(itemId) : undefined;` refuses anything that is not the selection. The 'epic' case of screenBody (board-state.ts:387-393) never calls detailsOf. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-state.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-host.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/details-memory.ts]

findings.premise: renderStages today draws the totals line first and returns early on the no-matches panel, so the records box must be appended before both to survive an empty filter result.
findings.evidence: board-host.ts:186: `function renderStages(b){renderTotals(b.totalsLabel,b.showAll);if(b.emptyPanel!==null){renderPanel(bodyEl,b.emptyPanel);return;}`. bodyEl is cleared before the switch at board-host.ts:296-297, so appending first puts the box at the top of the body. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-host.ts]

findings.premise: recordOwnerId, EpicRecordsView and StagesBody.epicRecords do not exist yet.
findings.evidence: Grep for `currentItemId|recordOwnerId|epicRecords` over vscode-plugin returns only currentItemId (board-state.ts:118, board-host.ts:41 and 536). StagesBody (board-protocol.ts:229-240) has kind, epic, totalsLabel, showAll, sections, fold, emptyPanel only. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-protocol.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-state.ts]

findings.premise: The reused pieces have the stated shape: memory.model builds details for any item (an Epic included) and attaches the opened record only for the memory's selection; detailsOf is null only when the item is not in the snapshot; recordsTable reads only d.evidence and d.itemId.
findings.evidence: details-memory.ts:136-142: `const record = snap === snapshot && itemId === selected ? opened : null; return buildItemDetails(snap, itemId, plan, record, deps.labels);`. board-details.ts:200-201 returns null only when `byId.get(itemId)` is undefined, and line 215 maps `item.evidence.map(e => evidenceRow(e, labels))` with no kind check. board-host.ts:534 passes `id => (shown === null ? null : memory.model(shown, id))`. recordsTable (board-host.ts:246-252) touches only `d.evidence` and `d.itemId`. OpenedRecord is exported from board-details.ts:37 and EvidenceRowView from board-protocol.ts:159. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/details-memory.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-details.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-host.ts]
findings.action: None. Note for the build: apply() derives the messages before memory.kept (board-host.ts:534-536), so the first render of an Epic's board has no opened record, which is correct; the record appears on the rerender after readRecord, as for a Story.

findings.premise: memory.kept(currentItemId(...)) is the single call site to change in the host, and currentItemId 'stays as it is for its other users'.
findings.evidence: The single-call-site part is true: the only use of currentItemId outside its definition is board-host.ts:536 (plus its import at line 41). The 'other users' wording is inaccurate: a grep over vscode-plugin finds no other user, in source or tests, so after the change currentItemId is an unused export and the import at board-host.ts:41 becomes unused. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-host.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-state.ts]
findings.action: In the build, drop the unused import in board-host.ts and either remove currentItemId or define recordOwnerId in terms of it; also update the host's header comment (board-host.ts:30-33, 'null on any other screen') and the details-memory header, which say the selection is a story or issue.

findings.premise: The inventory for the required field StagesBody.epicRecords is complete: one constructor (buildBoardViewModel) plus the spread in the 'epic' case.
findings.evidence: Grep for `kind: 'stages'` finds one object literal, board-model.ts:367. board-state.ts:392 spreads it (`{ ...body, epic: epicRowOf(...) }`). The tests import StagesBody as a type only (board-state.test.ts:51, board-host.test.ts:92, board-model.test.ts:18, board-views.test.ts:27) and build none by hand; no test deep-compares a whole StagesBody. The webview reads it in renderStages only (board-host.ts:186, 295). [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-model.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-state.ts]

findings.premise: Selecting an Epic in the memory reads no plan.
findings.evidence: details-memory.ts:51-52: `if (item === undefined || item.kind !== 'story') return null;` and kept() at 157-158 returns when `planId === null`; model() at 137-138 gives `{ state: 'none' }` for a null planId. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/details-memory.ts]

findings.premise: The change is a host-to-webview message shape only: nothing is stored, the daemon contract is untouched, and the host and webview cannot be at different versions.
findings.evidence: The webview script is a string constant in the host module (board-host.ts:87 `export const BOARD_WEBVIEW_SCRIPT`) set into the panel by renderBoardDocument (board-host.ts:475-498, 741), so both ends ship in one build. The down-message is rebuilt from state on every apply (board-host.ts:532-539) and never persisted; the webview keeps only density in vs.setState (board-host.ts:319-321). The evidence rows come from fields the snapshot already carries (delivery types.ts:274-283). [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-host.ts, src/workflow/delivery/types.ts]

findings.premise: The three open failures are detected and handled by existing code unchanged: a record that is not the selection's is refused and logged; with no review pane a reviewable record is read and shown read-only; a failed read becomes 'Could not read <id>: <message>'.
findings.evidence: details-memory.ts:164-169 (`log.warn('delivery board: ignored a request to open a record that is not the selected item\'s evidence'); return;`), 172 (`entry.openWith === 'review-view' && entry.mdPath !== null && deps.reviewPane !== undefined` else falls to readRecord), 94-98 (a throw becomes a typed read-failed result) and 127-129 (`text = `Could not read ${artifactId}: ${result.failure.message}``). None of these branches on the item's kind, so they apply to an Epic selection as written. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/details-memory.ts]

findings.premise: The stated edge behaviour is what the memory does: a selection or snapshot change drops the opened record and any read in flight; opening another record in the review pane leaves the read-only record shown; changing the search or filter on the Epic's board keeps it.
findings.evidence: details-memory.ts:146-156: a new snapshot or `selectedItemId !== selected` sets `opened = null; epoch++`. Line 123 drops a late answer (`madeAt !== epoch`). Lines 171-175: the review-pane branch bumps epoch and returns without clearing `opened`. set-search/set-attention keep the same trail entry and epic id (board-state.ts:208-213), so recordOwnerId is unchanged and kept() clears nothing. A removed Epic cuts the trail (board-state.ts:136, 147-154), which changes the selection. [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/details-memory.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/board-state.ts]

findings.premise: Each acceptance criterion maps to a named test that the existing test tooling can carry: the webview harness and the fixtures exist and can build an Epic with evidence.
findings.evidence: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/__tests__/ contains board-webview-harness.ts, board-fixtures.ts, board-state.test.ts, details-memory.test.ts and board-host.test.ts. board-fixtures.ts:25-29 `item(spec)` accepts any kind and evidence, and :54-56 `evidence(artifactId, kind, over)` defaults to `mdPath: null, openWith: 'evidence-read'` with overrides for a review-view record; largeSnapshot already builds `kind: 'epic'` items (:78). The mapping table covers ac1 (state + webview), ac2 (record owner + memory + host) and ac3 (unchanged-screens test + whole suite). [files: vscode-plugin/src/delivery/__tests__/board-fixtures.ts, vscode-plugin/src/delivery/__tests__/board-webview-harness.ts]
findings.action: None. For ac3, make the 'built exactly as before' test compare a Story's body and a list screen's body field by field (a list StagesBody now differs only by epicRecords: null), since the whole-suite check alone would not catch a new regression on the issue screen.

summary.prose: On the delivery board, an Epic's own screen now lists the Epic's records (its definition, its high-level design, amendments and spec) with their approval and review state, above the Epic's stages. Each row has the same button a Story's record has: a record that can be reviewed opens in the document review pane, with its diagrams and mocks as tabs; any other opens read-only under the table. Acceptance: ac1, an Epic's board lists the Epic's own records with their approval and review state, also when the Epic has no stories or no story matches the filter; ac2, a row's button opens the record in the review pane when it can be reviewed and read-only on the board otherwise; ac3, Stories' and issues' screens and the list screens are unchanged.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone Story — no parent HLD. Designed directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Delivery board: an Epic's own records on its board screen, opened as a Story's are

api.name: recordOwnerId

parameters.name: selection
parameters.purpose: The board's current selection (its trail of screens).

returns.meaning: The id of the item whose records are on show: the item of an 'item' screen, the Epic of an 'epic' screen, null on a list screen. New, in board-state.ts beside currentItemId, which stays as it is for its other users. createDeliveryBoardHost passes recordOwnerId(next.selection) to memory.kept in place of currentItemId(next.selection); that is the only change in the host's TypeScript.

preconditions: The selection has a current entry, as it always does
postconditions: On an item screen it returns what currentItemId returns
On an Epic's board the memory's selection is the Epic's id, so openEvidence accepts a record of that Epic and refuses any other
Leaving the Epic's board for a Story, another Epic or a list changes the selection, so the memory drops the opened record as it does today on any change of selection
An Epic selection reads no plan: planIdOf returns null for an item that is not a story

api.name: screenBodyOf (the 'epic' case)
api.signature: case 'epic': body = { ...buildBoardViewModel(snapshot, scope epic, paging, labels), epic: epicRowOf(...), epicRecords: epicRecordsOf(detailsOf(epic.id)) }

parameters.name: detailsOf
parameters.purpose: The existing callback the host gives boardDownMessages; it is memory.model over the shown snapshot, which builds details for any item, an Epic included, and attaches the opened record when the item is the memory's selection.

returns.meaning: The Epic's board as today plus epicRecords: { itemId: the Epic's id, evidence: the details' evidence rows (one per record of the Epic, in the snapshot's order), openedRecord: the details' opened record or null }. epicRecords is built from the Epic item alone, so the search text and the needs-attention filter do not change it. When detailsOf returns null (it does only when the item is not in the snapshot, and the case has already returned for that) epicRecords is null. buildBoardViewModel sets epicRecords: null, so All work and Standalone carry none.

errors.condition: An Epic with no evidence gives an empty rows list; the webview then says 'No records yet.' as a Story's table does.

preconditions: The Epic is in the snapshot (the case returns null otherwise, as today)
postconditions: An Epic's board body carries the Epic's records whatever the filter
Every other screen's body is built as before; a StagesBody of a list screen has epicRecords null

api.name: renderStages (webview)

parameters.name: b.epicRecords
parameters.purpose: The Epic's records and the opened read-only record.

returns.meaning: A box of class 'epic-records' is drawn first in the body, BEFORE the totals line and before the early return for the no-matches panel, so the records are there when no story matches. It holds the existing recordsTable(box, d) (label 'Records', the table, or 'No records yet.'), whose buttons send { type: 'open-evidence', itemId: d.itemId, artifactId } with the Epic's id, and under it the opened record (label 'Record <id>' and its text in a pre), drawn by one function shared with a Story's recordsTab so the two cannot drift. All text is set with the webview's make(), which sets textContent.

errors.condition: A read-only record that cannot be read is shown as the memory's 'Could not read <id>: <message>' text under the table, as on a Story's tab.

preconditions: recordsTable reads only d.evidence and d.itemId, which EpicRecordsView has
postconditions: The table is above the totals and the stage sections on an Epic's board only
A Story's Workflow evidence tab is drawn as before

dataModelChanges.details: One required field, epicRecords: EpicRecordsView | null. null on All work and Standalone; the Epic's records on an Epic's board. Host-to-webview message shape only; nothing is stored and the daemon contract is unchanged.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test run with tsx (npx tsx --test), as the plugin's delivery tests are; the webview is run through board-webview-harness.ts and snapshots come from board-fixtures.ts

migration.stateBefore: An Epic's board shows the Epic's header, the totals and the stages of its stories. The Epic's own records are in the snapshot but are shown nowhere, and the details memory has no selection on an Epic's board, so none of them can be opened.
migration.stateAfter: An Epic's board shows a Records table of the Epic's own records above the totals. The memory's selection is the Epic while its board is on show, so a row opens in the review pane or read-only as a Story's does.

migrationSteps.action: Add EpicRecordsView and StagesBody.epicRecords to the protocol; buildBoardViewModel sets it null; the 'epic' case of the screen body fills it from the details callback
Add recordOwnerId to board-state and pass it to memory.kept in the host in place of currentItemId
Draw the records box in the webview's renderStages, sharing the opened-record drawing with a Story's tab
Run the suite, build, package and install the plugin; check by hand

migration.backwardCompat: Plugin only. No daemon call, IPC shape or stored record changes; the host and the webview ship together in one plugin build, so the added message field has no version skew.

alternativesConsidered.name: Records table on the Epic's board
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The Epic's board screen shows the Epic's own records above its stages, opened the same way as a Story's
alternativesConsidered.approach: The Epic screen's body (StagesBody) gains epicRecords: the Epic item's id, its evidence rows (built by the existing evidenceRow through buildItemDetails) and the opened read-only record. board-state builds it for the 'epic' screen from the details the memory already gives for any item. The details memory is told the Epic is the selection while its board is on show (a new recordOwnerId replaces currentItemId at the one call site), so the existing openEvidence accepts the Epic's records unchanged: a reviewable one goes to the review pane, another is read and shown under the table. The webview draws the existing recordsTable in a box above the totals line.
pros: No daemon change: the snapshot already gives every Epic its DEF, HLD, AMD and SPEC with how each opens
Reuses the row builder, the table, the open-evidence message and the memory's open path; nothing is written twice
One place to look: the Epic's records are on the Epic's own screen
The memory's rule (only the selection's own records open) is kept, with the selection widened to the Epic on show
cons: The Epic's board grows by a small table above its stages
The memory's selection now means 'the item whose records are on show', not only 'the item screen's item'
